adherence.reason: The piece is framed as a fictional narrative set amid the 1918 influenza pandemic and the First World War.
Nell is explicitly a volunteer nurse tending influenza patients in a severely overcrowded field hospital.
She writes patient names in hymnbook margins and calls it a private ledger, but the text never establishes that she does so because she cannot bear a formal ledger of the dead.

A later section centers on a gauze shortage during a labeled 36-hour shift, but the overall story ranges across weeks and into 1919, and the focused episode itself does not clearly cover thirty-six hours.
Most immediate action uses present tense, but several narrative passages shift into past or past-perfect constructions, so the entire story is not consistently present tense.
The final section explicitly reveals Nell concealing her fever, cough, and chest tightness so she can remain on duty.
The final moment has Nell collapse at her post exactly as Grace and the relief shift arrive.
